note: Starter data tuned for warm/subtropical climates. Edit sow_months, temps, water_every_days and problems for your region - the app only trusts this file. Problem tips are general starter advice; confirm with a local agricultural extension service.

fruiting.name: Sown
fruiting.look_for: Soil is moist, not waterlogged. Nothing visible yet.

fruiting.name: Germinated
fruiting.look_for: Tiny green shoots breaking the soil. Count how many seeds came up.

fruiting.name: True leaves
fruiting.look_for: Second set of leaves (shaped like the adult plant). Thin crowded seedlings.

fruiting.name: Flowering
fruiting.look_for: Small flower buds or open flowers. Look for bees visiting.

fruiting.name: Fruit setting
fruiting.look_for: Tiny fruits forming where flowers dropped. Check leaves for pests.

fruiting.name: Harvest
fruiting.look_for: Fruit is full size and colour. Pick gently.

leafy.name: Sown
leafy.look_for: Soil is moist and cool. Nothing visible yet.

leafy.name: Germinated
leafy.look_for: Tiny green shoots. Keep soil damp.

leafy.name: Leafy growth
leafy.look_for: Several full leaves. Check undersides for insects.

leafy.name: Harvest
leafy.look_for: Leaves are full size. Cut outer leaves first.

root.name: Sown
root.look_for: Soil is loose and moist. Nothing visible yet.

root.name: Germinated
root.look_for: Feathery green tops appearing in rows.

root.name: Thinning
root.look_for: Crowded tops - thin so roots have room.

root.name: Root swelling
root.look_for: Shoulder of the root visible at soil level.

root.name: Harvest
root.look_for: Roots are full size. Loosen soil and pull gently.

flower.name: Sown
flower.look_for: Soil is moist. Nothing visible yet.

flower.name: Germinated
flower.look_for: Tiny green shoots with two round seed leaves.

flower.name: True leaves
flower.look_for: Frilly adult leaves. Pinch the tip for a bushier plant.

flower.name: Buds
flower.look_for: Flower buds forming. Look for pollinators.

flower.name: Blooming
flower.look_for: Open flowers. Pick regularly to keep it blooming.

crops.name: Tomato
crops.water: Even moisture, water at the base
crops.method: Containers or raised beds with a stake or cage; mulch to hold moisture

problems.action: Check watering - too much and too little both cause it. Remove badly yellowed leaves and keep leaves dry when watering.
Likely aphids or whiteflies. Spray them off with water and check leaf undersides daily.

crops.name: Chilli
crops.water: Moderate, let top soil dry between waterings
crops.method: Containers work well; pinch the first flowers for a bushier plant

problems.action: Can be heat stress, thrips or mites. Check leaf undersides, water in the morning and shade in extreme heat.
Often heat or uneven watering. Keep watering steady and avoid over-fertilising.

crops.name: Brinjal (Eggplant)
crops.method: Raised beds with mulch; stake once fruits get heavy

problems.action: Look for beetles or caterpillars and pick them off by hand in the morning.

problems.sign: Wilting even though soil is moist
problems.action: Could be a disease. Remove the affected plant (do not compost it) to protect neighbours, and rotate the bed next season.

crops.name: Okra
crops.method: Direct sow in rows; soak seeds overnight first

problems.action: Can be a viral disease spread by whiteflies. Remove badly affected plants, control whiteflies and avoid replanting okra in the same spot.
Harvest pods while still tender - leaving them on slows new pods.

crops.name: Cucumber
crops.method: Trellis it vertically to save space and keep fruit clean

problems.action: Likely powdery mildew. Water at the base, improve airflow and remove the worst leaves.
Usually uneven watering or heat stress. Water evenly and pick fruit regularly.

crops.name: Bottle gourd
crops.method: Grow on an overhead trellis; the vines are vigorous

problems.action: Often a pollination issue. Look for bees, or hand-pollinate in the morning by moving pollen from a male flower to a female flower (the one with a tiny fruit at its base).
Likely powdery mildew. Water at the base, improve airflow and remove the worst leaves.

crops.name: Beans
crops.method: Direct sow beside a pole or string for climbing

problems.action: Check drainage - waterlogged soil is a common cause. Avoid touching plants when leaves are wet.
Check undersides for aphids or caterpillars. Remove by hand or spray off with water.

crops.name: Spinach
crops.method: Broadcast or row sow; succession-sow every 2 weeks

problems.sign: Plant sending up a flower stalk (bolting)
problems.action: Usually heat or long days. Harvest what you can and sow again in a cooler period.
Look for leaf miners or caterpillars. Remove affected leaves and pick off pests by hand.

crops.name: Coriander
crops.method: Crush seeds lightly before sowing; grows well in shallow pots

problems.sign: Flowering and going to seed quickly
problems.action: Heat makes coriander bolt. Give afternoon shade and sow small batches every 2 weeks.

problems.sign: Seedlings falling over at soil level
problems.action: Likely damping off from overwatering. Water less, improve drainage and avoid sowing too densely.

crops.name: Fenugreek (Methi)
crops.method: Scatter seeds densely in a tray or bed; fast and beginner friendly

problems.action: Check for waterlogged soil and avoid overwatering.
Likely powdery mildew. Water at the base, improve airflow and remove the worst leaves.

crops.name: Lettuce
crops.method: Shallow containers; harvest outer leaves to keep it producing

problems.action: Heat is making it bolt. Give afternoon shade and harvest early.
Slugs or snails. Check at dusk or dawn and remove by hand.

crops.name: Radish
crops.method: Direct sow in rows; the fastest crop for a first harvest

problems.sign: Lots of leaf, small or no roots
problems.action: Often crowding, too much shade or too much nitrogen. Thin seedlings and give several hours of sun.
Uneven watering or leaving them too long. Water evenly and harvest on time.

crops.name: Carrot
crops.method: Direct sow in deep pots or beds; thin seedlings to 3 cm apart

problems.action: Stones or hard soil. Loosen the soil deeper before the next sowing.
Carrot seeds are slow, often 1-3 weeks. Keep the surface moist and do not let a crust form.

crops.name: Marigold
crops.method: Plant near vegetables; the flowers help deter some pests

problems.action: Possible spider mites in hot, dry weather. Spray leaves with water, especially undersides.
Usually too little sun or too much fertiliser. Move to full sun and remove spent blooms.
